hpi_details: 65M with a history of prior appendectomy presents with 2 days of diffuse crampy abdominal pain, bilious vomiting, abdominal distension, and inability to pass flatus or stool.

investigation_events.title: STAT small-bowel obstruction results
investigation_events.availability_message: The STAT small-bowel obstruction results are now available; nasogastric decompression, IV fluids, and surgical consultation should not be delayed.

results.test: CT abdomen and pelvis with IV contrast
results.value: Dilated small-bowel loops up to 4.0 cm with a transition point in the right lower quadrant near the prior operative site; no pneumatosis or free air

core_concepts: Adhesions are the most common cause in patients with prior abdominal surgery.
common_misconceptions: Assuming passing a small amount of gas completely rules out obstruction.
dangerous_errors: Missing signs of strangulation (fever, tachycardia, localized tenderness).
management_principles: NPO, NG tube decompression, IV fluids, serial exams.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

source_refs.title: SAGES & ACS Evidence-Based Surgical Practice Guidelines

reference_soap.subjective: 65M with obstipation, vomiting, and prior surgery.
reference_soap.objective: Distended, tympanic abdomen, high-pitched bowel sounds.
reference_soap.plan: CT abdomen/pelvis, NG tube, NPO, surgical consult.

learning_objectives: Recognize signs of SBO and indications for NG tube.

teaching.one_liner: Classic presentation of adhesive small bowel obstruction with vomiting, distension, and obstipation in a patient with prior abdominal surgery.

must_ask.say: Have you been able to pass gas or have a bowel movement?
Have you been vomiting? What does it look like — is it greenish or bile-colored?
Have you had any abdominal surgery in the past, such as an appendectomy?
Has your belly become swollen or bloated?
Is the pain crampy and coming in waves, and has it changed over the last two days?

history.answer: Doctor, I've had terrible cramping belly pain and I can't stop throwing up.
It started two days ago all of a sudden, and the cramps have gotten progressively worse.
I threw up four or five times yesterday and three times today, usually twenty to thirty minutes after trying to drink something.
At first it was undigested food, but now it's dark greenish-yellow bitter liquid without any blood or foul stool smell.
No, it isn't shooting out like a projectile, and it happens whenever I drink rather than just in the morning.
The cramping is all over my belly, and throwing up doesn't make the pain go away.
I haven't passed any stool or even passed gas since yesterday, and I definitely don't have diarrhea.
My stomach has swollen up a lot over the past two days, feeling bloated like a drum.
No, I haven't had any fever, chills, or sweats, and my wife ate the exact same dinner and feels completely fine.
No headache, neck stiffness, dizziness, blurry vision, or confusion at all.
No, I haven't fallen, hit my head, or suffered any injury recently.
I can't keep any liquids down right now, my mouth feels dry, and I've only passed a tiny amount of dark urine today.
No, I haven't noticed excessive thirst or frequent urination before this, and I don't have diabetes or take insulin.
No chest pressure, chest pain, or shortness of breath.
I haven't started any new medications, I don't drink alcohol, and I've never used marijuana or recreational drugs.
No, my weight has been completely steady before getting sick two days ago.
No, absolutely not; my stomach just heaves on its own and forces everything up.
I feel like my intestines are completely blocked and nothing can move through.
I'm really terrified that I might need an emergency operation to fix this.
I just want this terrible cramping and throwing up to stop so I can get some relief.
I have been healthy overall and don't have high blood pressure, heart disease, or stomach ulcers.
I had an open appendectomy about twenty years ago, but I haven't had any other surgeries or hospital stays since.
I don't take any prescription medicines, over-the-counter pills, or herbal supplements.
I don't have any known allergies to medicines or foods.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used any tobacco products.
I don't drink any beer, wine, or liquor.
I'm a retired schoolteacher and I live at home with my wife.
My father had high blood pressure and my mother lived to ninety, with no history of bowel problems or cancer in my family.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 116/74 mmHg, pulse 88 beats per minute, respiratory rate 18 breaths per minute, body temperature 36.8°C, oxygen saturation 98% on room air.
Dry oral mucosa with dry lips; posterior pharynx is clear without erythema or exudates.
Alert, oriented to person, place, and time, appearing uncomfortable due to intermittent abdominal cramping.
Supple neck with full active range of motion; negative Kernig and Brudzinski signs.
Distended and symmetrically rounded abdomen with a well-healed surgical scar in the right lower quadrant; no visible peristalsis.
High-pitched, hyperactive tinkling bowel sounds with intermittent rushes.
Generalized tympany on percussion throughout all four quadrants; no shifting dullness.
Diffuse mild tenderness on palpation across all quadrants without guarding or muscular rigidity.
No rebound tenderness elicited in any quadrant.
No reducible or incarcerated femoral or inguinal hernias bilaterally.
Empty rectal vault with no palpable masses or tenderness; no gross blood on examining glove.
Decreased skin turgor with slightly delayed skin recoil; capillary refill time is normal under two seconds.
